T usually + adv/prep: › to push a loose end of a piece of clothing or material into a particular place or position, especially to make it tidy or comfortable
› to put something into a safe or convenient place
› to hold part of your body in a particular position
› to be in a place that is hidden or where few people go

C: › [ C ] a narrow fold sewn into something, especially a piece of material, either for decoration or to change its shape
（用於裝飾或改變形狀的）褶；打褶
› [ C ] an operation to remove unwanted fat from a part of the body

U: › [ U ] UK old-fashioned child's word food, especially sweets and cakes

example: Should I tuck my shirt into my trousers?
我應該把襯衫下擺塞進褲子裡嗎？
He tucked the bottom of the sheet under the mattress.
他把床單邊緣塞入床墊下。
Tuck your gloves in your pocket so that you don't lose them.
把手套放進口袋裡，這樣就不會弄丟了。
She had a doll tucked under her arm.
她把玩具娃娃夾在胳膊下。
Eventually I found the certificate tucked under a pile of old bills.
最後我發現證書壓在一堆舊帳單下。
Tuck your chair in (= put it so that the seat of it is under the table) so that no one trips over it.
把你的椅子推到桌下，以防絆倒人。
Stand up straight, tuck your tummy in and tuck your bottom under.
站直了，收腹提臀。
She sat with her legs tucked under her.
她盤腿坐著。
Tucked along/down this alley are some beautiful old houses.
這條巷子的深處有一些漂亮的老房子。
A group of tiny brick houses is tucked away behind the factory.
工廠後面隱藏著一片小磚房。
a tummy tuck
腹部抽脂手術
a tuck shop
食品店
See also
tucker
Judging by the way they tucked into their dinner, they must have been very hungry.
看他們晚餐時那種狼吞虎嚥的樣子，一定是餓壞了。
There's plenty of food, so please tuck in.
食物充足，請盡情地吃吧。

NONE: › to make someone comfortable in bed, especially a child, by arranging the covers around them
給（孩子）掖好被子；將（孩子）在床上安頓好

example: Daddy, if I go to bed now will you tuck me in?
爸爸，要是我現在去睡覺，你會幫我掖被子嗎？
The children are safely tucked up in bed.
孩子們安逸地躺在被子裡。

NONE: › to put something in a private, safe place

example: Grandma always kept a little of money tucked away in case of an emergency.
奶奶總是藏點錢以備急用。
a tucker bag
食品袋
